# Undo after a native popup close empties the other popup's window

## Context

Found by the gate-3 non-author walk of `apps/workstation` on the v13.3.1 candidate `e2f77dd0fb` (receipt on #20022, finding 3). Ordinary pointer and window input in headed Chrome, standalone Workstation. First recorded as "by design" (the DockLayoutsWindows guide: "Redo puts it back in the same window", #19583's note); promoted to a milestone bug by the operator's ruling of 2026-10-23 (~14:00 CEST): the version handed to the external tester carries no known bug, and a blank window left on screen is one from the user's seat.

Design authority: the operator's ruling above overrides the guide's window retention for the case where an Undo empties a visible popup window.

## The Problem

Two panes popped out (`100k Matrix` → window A, `Distributed Trace Explorer` → window B, both at the default origin). Close A natively (its pane does not return — #20045). Click Undo:

- B's pane docks back into main (`Distributed Trace Explorer` active in the main strip, Undo 2 / Redo 1);
- **B's window stays open and blank** (body empty, 56 DOM nodes, 955×499 at the origin) — the user closed A and watches B go empty;
- Redo refills B's window with its pane.

Reproduced in session a (gestures 17–21). The Undo targets the most recent history row, which is B's pop-out, because A's close never became a row (#20045 part A).

## The Architectural Reality (inference, to be verified by the owner)

- `PopupWorkspace.projectDockCommit` reopens before projection on Undo and Redo closes the exact current window (#19292); window retention across Undo/Redo is deliberate so Redo lands in the same window (#19583's Undo-reopened path; the guide's station).
- The retention is invisible when the emptied window is parked behind main; here both popups sit at the main window's origin in front of it, so the blank window is the most visible thing on screen.

## The Fix (prescription, owner's call)

When an Undo empties a popup window, do not leave it visible blank: close it (Redo re-opens a window through the existing re-open path) or hide it and close it at lease expiry. Keep the Undo/Redo pair correct either way. Also worth the owner's look: Undo after a native close should target the close, which is #20045 part A's fix — with it, this case changes shape (A's pane returns, B is untouched); this ticket still holds for any Undo that empties a visible popup.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: red-first e2e arm (two pop-outs, close A natively, Undo via the toolbar button): no open popup window without content remains visible 1 s after the Undo on `e2f77dd0fb` → red; green at head.
- [ ] AC-2: Redo after that Undo shows B's pane in a window again (same or re-opened), with its content.
- [ ] AC-3: the guide's station on Undo/Redo window retention states the new behaviour.
- [ ] AC-4 (post-merge): one full local `e2e/workstation` + `e2e/dashboard` run green.

## Out of Scope

#20045 (the native close losing its pane; the wedge after Undo); the default popup geometry stacking every popup at the origin (a separate design question, not filed).

The two-popup arm no longer closes a window: it undoes the second pop-out directly, the state an unrecorded close left behind, so it keeps its meaning once a bare target close is recorded. The close a user makes (beforeunload) is its own arm, which first asserts that the close is one history row: undoing that row re-opens the popup while the other keeps its pane. Both emptying arms assert the close within 1000 ms of the Undo click. Pop-outs go through the shared workstationPopOut choreography and panes are addressed by their live id."

* fix(dock): an undo or redo keeps a popup's window in step with its document (#20047)

replayWorkspaceReturn embodied on undo and closed on redo only for the native-close return row, so undoing a pop-out sent the pane home and left its popup on screen blank until redo refilled it. Every undo and redo a popup receives now follows one rule: a replay that empties a bound popup closes its window after projection, and one that fills a popup without a window embodies it first. The return row's two branches are instances of the rule; only participants with a close policy are touched, so the root's window never is.
